analysis: The recency-weighted LightGCN trial completed successfully but did not improve reported macro validation HR@10: 0.5537, matching the prior result. Electronics declined from 0.335 to 0.330, so this experiment does not support recency weighting as a remedy for its weaker performance. Current category HR@10 values were Movies_and_TV 0.600, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.610, Electronics 0.330, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.675. Training and generated-predictor consistency checks passed for repeated items, padding, singleton histories, and empty histories. Implementation consistency does not establish a recommendation-quality gain; no test metrics were available.
code_summary: LightGCN uses 64-dimensional embeddings and averages the initial embeddings with two graph propagation layers. The graph retains unique user-item edges with symmetric degree normalization. User representations combine the propagated user vector with 0.5 times a history profile. This trial weights every chronological history occurrence with a 10-interaction half-life, normalizes per history, and sums repeated-item contributions. Exported inference applies the same weighting using masks and complete histories. BPR loss, Adam, regularization, sampling, validation checkpoint selection with NDCG@10 tie-breaking, early stopping, all four dataset routes, and trial-local artifacts remain unchanged. The predictor loads materialized user/item embeddings from each category checkpoint.
